guardian.title: Babies born to anaemic mothers have smaller brains, study finds
guardian.description:
Key regions of the brain linked to movement, learning and emotions were affected and may lead to cognitive problems

Babies born to mothers with anaemia have smaller brains, particularly in key regions linked to movement, learning and the regulation of emotion, according to a study.

Researchers said the differences, first detected at the age of one, could lead to cognitive problems when children started school.

US-Israel war on Iran and political instability in Somalia lead to pirates targeting cargo ships off Horn of Africa

The scourge of Somali piracy targeting cargo ships and smaller dhows off the Horn of Africa has returned to levels not seen in a decade, driven by a convergence of factors including disruptions to the shipping industry caused by the US-Israeli war against Iran and a resurgence of political instability in Somalia.

Torrential rain causes widespread damage; while north-west South Africa hit by thunderstorms and central-southern US faces oppressive heat

Typhoon Saudel brought days of torrential rain to Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Fujian and Guangdong provinces in south-east China last week. guardian.title: Egyptian TV presenter among 12 sentenced to death for drug crime
guardian.description:
Sarah Khalifa, 39, charged with forming organised criminal gang to manufacture and traffic drugs

An Egyptian court sentenced a well-known television presenter and 11 others to death for manufacturing and trafficking narcotics in a sprawling drug case, official media reported on Saturday.

The presenter, Sarah Khalifa, 39, is best known for her programme Mission Impossible, which dealt with issues concerning security and crime.

guardian.description:
Togo-sponsored resolution called to phase out traditional map that depicts continent as similar size to Greenland

The United Nations has voted to adopt a resolution for the world to formally phase out the traditional Mercator map of the globe in favour of one that more accurately displays Africa’s size.

guardian.title: Family of British man found dead in Grenada ask local police to work with UK investigators
guardian.description:
Andrew Frederick’s body was found in property he was staying at in Grenada in January

The family of a British father who was found dead in the Caribbean in January is urging authorities in Grenada to work with UK police to uncover the truth about his death.

Andrew Frederick’s body was found in the property he was staying at in Grenada on 4 January. An autopsy, performed in the same week by a privately hired pathologist, concluded that the 47-year-old’s death was a homicide.

Three men are on trial over the death of brothers Jake and Callum Robinson and their friend, US citizen Jack Carter Rhoad, in Ensenada

The father of two Australian surfers killed in Mexico two years ago testified in court on Tuesday that his life had been turned into hell, as the high-profile trial continued into its second day.

guardian.title: Jamaican delegates arrive in UK to hand slavery reparations petition to King Charles
guardian.description:
Slavery’s legacy continues ‘to deprive our country and our people’, says minister, as group prepares to appeal to Jamaica’s head of state

A landmark petition is to be handed to King Charles by Jamaica over slavery reparations, aiming to confront historical crimes that still disadvantage former British colonies, the Caribbean nation’s culture minister has said.

The petition will be lodged with Charles, Jamaica’s head of state, on Monday.

guardian.title: Singapore boosts PM’s salary by $1m amid major pay rise for ministers
guardian.description:
The affluent city-state has justified high-end salaries for its political leaders, arguing they attract talent and ensure good governance

Singapore’s prime minister has been given a $1m pay rise as the affluent city-state announced a dramatic one-off salary boost for government ministers.

The pay increases add more than 60% to what are already the world’s highest ministerial salaries.

guardian.description:
Shinjuku ward targets accommodation in residential areas and near cultural sites as locals complain visitors disposing of rubbish improperly and being too noisy

A neighbourhood in Tokyo popular with foreign tourists will ban visitors from using thousands of short-term rental accommodations after a slew of complaints about behaviour.

guardian.description:
Connection across Tumen River is further sign of closer ties between the two countries since start of war in Ukraine

Beijing wants banks and insurers to bolster investment in stock market as it helps to replenish cash reserves

China will inject $54bn (£40bn) into its financial sector as Beijing attempts to shore up banks and insurers in the face of faltering economic growth.

A host of financial institutions said they were due to receive billions of yuan in capital from state institutions including the ministry of finance and even the company that runs the country’s tobacco monopoly.

euronews.description: The link between consuming very hot drinks and oesophageal cancer has been established by the world’s largest study into the subject yet.

euronews.description: The EU has introduced a framework to support long-term rentals in tourist-heavy cities. Airbnb warns it creates regulatory uncertainty without improving long-term housing outcomes.

euronews.title: Would you let AI design your next tattoo? Tattoo artists say AI is changing the way they work
euronews.description: Customers are increasingly using generative AI to visualise tattoo ideas, while artists use it for photo restoration and design references.

euronews.title: Egypt, Greece and Cyprus back plans to bring Cypriot gas to Europe
euronews.description: Cyprus’ Cronos gas is expected to reach European markets via Egypt from 2028, with Greece offering an onward route into southeastern and central Europe. The three countries renewed their backing for the plan at their El Alamein summit.

euronews.title: Russian hackers may have used fake CAPTCHA to hack Ukrainian government computers
euronews.description: Researchers say the attack was likely part of a wider operation to steal cryptocurrency and login credentials by tricking users through a fake Google verification check to trick victims.

euronews.title: EU to give cities more power to curb Airbnb and short-term rentals
euronews.description: "Short-term rental activity" grew 93 percent across four major letting platforms between 2018 and 2024, according to the EU.

euronews.title: Hungary takes one more step to normalise relations with Brussels over rule of law
euronews.description: Hungary has formally notified Brussels it has met its rule-of-law conditions, a step that could unlock €4.2bn in EU funds and restore access for researchers and students who were left out of European programs.

euronews.title: When war takes away the classroom, can children ever catch up?
euronews.description: Attacks on education have surged worldwide. Education Above All Foundation's Dr Maleiha Malik says keeping children learning is possible, but conflict-caused damage cannot be undone easily.

euronews.title: France co-hosts major space summit with Germany despite US firms' withdrawals and Merz absence
euronews.description: France is co-hosting a major space summit with Germany this week, as Europe finds itself at a strategic crossroads.

euronews.title: China reiterates its One China principle on Taiwan over UN resolution
euronews.description: Beijing reaffirmed its One-China principle following a renewed dispute over the interpretation of a UN resolution that defined lawful representation of China at the world's foremost intergovernmental body.

euronews.title: Braga celebrates African heritage over two days with music, film and debates
euronews.description: The festival celebrates African heritage, between the "culture we inherit" and the "reality we build". It takes place on 11 and 12 September in Braga.

euronews.title: Spain’s football federation backs fertility treatment for players and referees
euronews.description: Elite players in Spain’s women’s national team and staff to be given access to fertility treatments to ease up pressure and better plan if or when to become mothers. The decision comes as Europe grapples with falling fertility rates.

euronews.title: Meet Nazym Kyzaibay, Kazakhstan’s first female world boxing champion and Olympic bronze medallist
euronews.description: Nazym Kyzaibay recounts her rise from a young boxer to Central Asia’s first female three-time world boxing champion and an Olympic bronze medallist.

euronews.title: Albania, Hong Kong and Egypt tipped as the trending destinations to watch in 2027
euronews.description: New data predicts which destinations are tipped to take off in 2027, with major sporting events and a spectacular solar eclipse also set to shape where travellers choose to go next year.

lemonde.title: « Une maison d’édition, c’est d’abord un refuge » : des écrivains racontent leur départ de Grasset, propriété de Vincent Bolloré
lemonde.description: Dans « La Grande Evasion », un ouvrage collectif à paraître le 10 septembre chez Buchet-Chastel, des écrivains qui ont quitté Grasset après l’éviction d’Olivier Nora évoquent leur relation à leur ancien éditeur et leur « métier bizarre, où l’on reste chez soi des mois devant un écran ».

lemonde.title: Au Venezuela, le sulfureux Alejandro Betancourt, l’homme derrière « le plus gros contrat pétrolier de l’histoire mondiale »
lemonde.description: A la tête de la North American Blue Energy Partners, le milliardaire de 46 ans, choisi comme partenaire par l’administration Trump pour exploiter les ressources pétrolières du pays, est visé par des enquêtes pour blanchiment et fraude fiscale en Suisse et en Espagne.

lemonde.title: Au Népal, quinze jours après la catastrophe, les autorités espèrent toujours trouver des survivants
lemonde.description: Le bilan de la crue soudaine et dévastatrice provoquée le 26 août par un glissement de terrain en haute altitude s’établit, au 9 septembre, à 1 410 morts et 5 651 disparus. Le relief accidenté et l’ampleur des destructions rendent difficile l’acheminement de l’aide.

lemonde.title: Budget 2027 : Sébastien Lecornu lance une « opération déminage » auprès des chefs d’entreprise en promettant une baisse de la contribution exceptionnelle
lemonde.description: A trois semaines de la présentation du projet de loi de finances 2027, le premier ministre confirme que la surtaxe « exceptionnelle » sur les grandes entreprises ne va pas disparaître. Mais elle devrait baisser, et un nouveau dispositif être créé pour favoriser la reprise d’entreprises par les salariés.

lemonde.title: L’Iran condamne les frappes américaines et instaure une nouvelle « zone interdite » près du détroit d’Ormuz
lemonde.description: Téhéran dénonce les frappes américaines contre ses pétroliers et pose ses conditions pour mettre fin à la guerre, alors que les tirs se poursuivent autour du détroit d’Ormuz malgré le cessez-le-feu d’avril.

lemonde.title: « Hair, Paper, Water… », le fabuleux film à la lisière des grottes de Nicolas Graux et Minh Quy Truong
lemonde.description: Au Vietnam, les cinéastes brossent le portrait impressionniste de Cao Thi Hâu, issue d’une ethnie en perdition, transmettant sa culture à son petit-fils.

lemonde.title: Le chercheur Emmanuel Mignot reçoit le prix Lasker pour ses travaux sur la narcolepsie
lemonde.description: Depuis la fin des années 1980 à l’université Stanford, le psychiatre et pharmacologue français explore les causes de ce trouble du sommeil invalidant. Il partage cette récompense américaine prestigieuse, attribuée mercredi 9 septembre, avec le Japonais Masashi Yanagisawa.

lemonde.title: Primaire du PS : le duel entre Olivier Faure et Raphaël Glucksmann électrise la campagne
lemonde.description: Les deux favoris s’affrontent sur les modalités de la primaire du camp social-démocrate. Le premier secrétaire du PS souhaite toujours un élargissement à de nouveaux candidats, comme François Ruffin ou Matthieu Pigasse. Ce que rejette l’eurodéputé Place publique.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : le Kremlin affirme qu’il n’existe actuellement aucune « feuille de route » pour un règlement du conflit
lemonde.description: Le porte-parole du Kremlin, Dmitri Peskov, a toutefois affirmé que Moscou espérait une reprise des négociations trilatérales dans un avenir proche, et a confirmé officiellement qu’un potentiel sommet trilatéral Russie - Chine - Etats-Unis avait été abordé lors de l’entretien téléphonique entre les chefs d’Etat russe et américain le 8 septembre.

lemonde.title: Carcassonne : une vidéo de policiers municipaux tenant des propos racistes et misogynes en pleine rue diffusée, le parquet ouvre une enquête
lemonde.description: Selon « Midi libre », qui a diffusé cette vidéo datant de 2025, le policier qui tient les propos les plus extrêmes est un ex-militaire, membre bénévole du service d’ordre de Jordan Bardella. Le RN a annoncé mercredi avoir « immédiatement procédé à sa radiation » du service et à son « exclusion » du parti.

lemonde.title: Visite du pape Léon XIV en France : l’Eglise et les autorités s’attendent à une affluence record
lemonde.description: Léon XIV doit se rendre en France du 25 au 28 septembre. Des centaines de milliers de fidèles sont attendus dans les rues de la capitale, où le souverain pontife passera deux jours, et 80 000 jeunes devraient participer à une veillée au Stade de France.

lemonde.title: Face aux IA, avoir un corps change tout
lemonde.description: La présentation visuelle d’un objet manipulable active notamment les aires prémotrices, observe Sylvie Chokron dans sa Carte blanche au « Monde », insistant sur l’importance de l’interaction entre le corps et l’action.

lemonde.title: Victoire de l’AfD : « Il y a fort à parier que l’onde de choc allemande amplifie en France des tendances europhobes déjà à l’œuvre »
lemonde.description: La victoire de l’AfD aux élections en Saxe-Anhalt, le 6 septembre, aura des conséquences sur les élections françaises et, au-delà, sur le lien franco-allemand, s’inquiète, dans une tribune au « Monde », l’historien Frédéric Bozo, professeur à l’université Sorbonne-Nouvelle.

lemonde.title: Violences dans le périscolaire à Paris : Anne Hidalgo partage la douleur des familles, sans s’excuser
lemonde.description: L’ex-maire de la capitale, visée par une plainte de familles dans le cadre du scandale des violences sexuelles dans le périscolaire, a dit mercredi regretter de ne pas les avoir rencontrées, sans toutefois présenter d’excuses, comme elles le réclamaient.

lemonde.title: La Commission européenne veut simplifier et « européaniser » les marchés publics
lemonde.description: Cette réforme doit permettre « la fin de la domination du critère prix », qui favorise de fait les produits chinois, estime Stéphane Séjourné, vice-président exécutif de la Commission européenne. L’ensemble des marchés publics dans l’Union européenne pèsent chaque année 2 600 milliards d’euros, soit 15 % du PIB.

lemonde.title: Immobilier : les prix baissent en région parisienne
lemonde.description: Alors que les ventes sont en hausse, les maisons ont perdu 1,5 % en un an, et les appartements 0,3 % en trois mois. Les notaires anticipent une légère augmentation d’ici à la fin de l’année, mais la possible remontée des taux d’intérêt pourrait fausser leurs prévisions.

rfi.title: French billionaire Olivier Bouygues faces suspended jail term over wildlife killings
rfi.description: French prosecutors are seeking a five-year suspended prison sentence for billionaire Olivier Bouygues over the killing of protected birds on his hunting estate in central France. Investigators found decomposing animal carcasses, banned traps and records of bonuses paid for animals killed at the 650-hectare property. Bouygues denies responsibility.

rfi.title: Macron hosts global space summit in Paris snubbed by US companies
rfi.description: French President Emmanuel Macron is hosting dozens of leaders, technology experts and scientists in Paris for a two-day global space summit that opens on Wednesday, as major US companies including SpaceX and Blue Origin stay away.

rfi.title: Heat forces French champagne makers to stiffen their drink
rfi.description: Drinking this year's champagne might give you a heftier headache as France's record heatwaves are forcing some producers to up the alcohol levels, industry officials said Wednesday.

rfi.title: France among 12 nations to sanction trade with Israeli settlements
rfi.description: Twelve countries, including Britain, Canada and France, said on Tuesday that they would impose sanctions on trade with Israeli settlements in the West Bank, following an increase in attacks by Israeli settlers against Palestinian villages in the occupied territory.

rfi.title: PSG boss Enrique urges squad to forget about past Champions League triumphs
rfi.description: PSG head coach Luis Enrique called on his Champions League-winning players to dismiss their back-to-back glories in the competition and re-motivate themselves for more success in European club football's most coveted competition.

rfi.title: French pupils fall to record low in global education survey
rfi.description: French students' results in the 2025 international Pisa survey are the lowest ever recorded, yet remain in line with the OECD average, according to results published on Tuesday. French Education Minister Édouard Geffray criticised social media as one of the causes, and pledged to focus on raising standards in middle schools over the next five-year term in order to close the gap.

rfi.title: Internal inquiry opened after Eiffel Tower 'sexist' closure prompts strike
rfi.description: The Eiffel Tower reopened on Tuesday after staff walked out over the removal of women colleagues during a visit by a Hindu religious group which later apologised. The operating company has acknowledged it was wrong to accept the conditions and has opened an internal investigation.

rfi.title: Hunt on for thieves after Renoir museum raid in southern France
rfi.description: A search is under way for the thieves who stole several paintings from a museum dedicated to the French Impressionist painter Pierre-Auguste Renoir in the south of France in the early hours of Tuesday morning.

rfi.title: French firefighters begin six-week strike over funding after record summer fires
rfi.description: French professional firefighters launch a six-week nationwide campaign on Tuesday, demanding more funding, staff and better protection for their health after a summer of unprecedented wildfires.

rfi.title: France tries 14 over deadliest Channel migrant crossing disaster
rfi.description: Fourteen people are to go on trial in France on Tuesday over the loss of 31 people including a seven-year-old child in 2021, in the deadliest small-boat crossing accident recorded in the Channel.

rfi.title: Dembélé leads PSG's nine-man charge for 2026 Ballon d'Or
rfi.description: The 2025 Ballon d'Or winner Ousmane Dembélé led the nine-strong Paris Saint-Germain contingent on the 30-player shortlist unveiled on Tuesday for the 2026 accolade as the world's best footballer.

rfi.title: Champions League kicks off with Lille, Lens eyeing PSG's crown
rfi.description: The 2026/27 Champions League gets under way on Tuesday night, with French clubs Lille and Lens among the 35 teams hoping to supplant Paris Saint-Germain as champions.

rfi.title: Merz ‘deeply shocked’ as far-right victory tests Germany’s political firewall
rfi.description: The fallout from the AfD’s landslide in Saxony-Anhalt is testing Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s reform agenda, Germany’s support for Ukraine and the political firewall designed to keep the far-right out of power.

rfi.title: EU chief unveils €200m Greenland package amid tensions over Trump claims
rfi.description: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen unveiled a 200-million-euro investment package for Greenland during the second of a two-day visit. The European Union has increased its focus on the vast, strategic island since President Donald Trump began insisting that the United States should take control of it for security reasons.

rfi.title: Sons of Yemen ex-president on trial in France over alleged stolen assets
rfi.description: Two sons of former Yemeni president Ali Abdullah Saleh are on trial in Paris on Monday, accused of embezzling public funds that were used to buy luxury property worth €16 million in Paris.

rfi.title: Jamaica steps up slavery reparations campaign with petition to King Charles III
rfi.description: Jamaica is testing a new legal route in its long-running campaign for slavery reparations, asking Britain’s monarch to put key questions before the Privy Council.

rfi.title: France, South Korea announce billion-euro investment for audiovisual industry
rfi.description: France and South Korea will invest one billion euros to support the audiovisual and entertainment sector, President Emmanuel Macron said as he brought together some of the world's top entertainment bosses for a summit on the future of cinema.

france24fr.title: "Je ne me sens plus en sécurité" : au Kenya, l'inquiétude des commerçants burundais
france24fr.description: Depuis les déclarations du président kényan William Ruto, lundi, stigmatisant les travailleurs étrangers, les Burundais manifestent leur colère. Ils sont 16 000 réfugiés et demandeurs d’asile burundais à vivre au Kenya, et beaucoup survivent grâce à des emplois dans le secteur informel. La très grande majorité d'entre eux cherche désormais à quitter le territoire.

france24fr.title: Camille Cottin et sa bande de retour dans "Dix pour cent, le film"
france24fr.description: Au programme de ce numéro 100 % cinéma de "À l'Affiche !" : "Dix pour cent, le film" d'Émilie Noblet. Six ans après la sortie de la quatrième saison de "Dix pour cent", les agents et leurs talents reviennent pour un film disponible sur Netflix. Camille Cottin, Laure Calamy, Grégory Montel, Nicolas Maury...toute la bande est là avec en "guest-stars" : George Clooney, Eva Longoria, Vincent Macaigne et Laetitia Casta.

france24fr.title: Tunisie : manifestations pour la libération du journaliste Mohamed Yousfi
france24fr.description: 🇹🇳 En Tunisie, les journalistes se mobilisent après l’arrestation de leur confrère Mohamed Yousfi. Interpellé vendredi avant une émission sur la crise de l’eau, il est soupçonné de blanchiment d’argent. Un mandat de dépôt a été émis contre lui mardi.

france24fr.title: Sanctions contre Israël : 12 personnalités britanniques interdites d'entrée sur le territoire
france24fr.description: Le Royaume-Uni, la France, le Canada et huit autres pays ont annoncé, mardi 8 septembre, qu'ils allaient sanctionner le commerce avec les colonies israéliennes en Cisjordanie, durcissant le ton face à Israël. L'État hébreu a riposté en annonçant la fermeture du consulat britannique à Jérusalem. Depuis, douze représentants britanniques ont l'interdiction d'entrer en Israël. Décryptage avec Anne Corpet, chroniqueuse internationale France 24.

france24fr.title: Pisa : la France au fond de la classe ? Parlons-en avec H. Duminil-Copin, T. Cojean et B. Larseneur
france24fr.description: Aujourd'hui dans "Parlons-en", on retourne sur les bancs de l'école en cette période de rentrée scolaire. Et le bulletin n'est pas bon pour les petits français. Le classement Pisa – qui classe le niveau des jeunes de 15 ans de l'OCDE tous les trois ans – est sorti mardi. Le constat est implacable : c'est la dégringolade pour les collégiens tricolores en maths, en sciences, en compréhension de l'écrit... Ils n'ont jamais été aussi peu performants. À qui la responsabilité ?

france24fr.title: "Un potentiel de très grands vins" : des bouteilles de champagne à plus de 13 % d'alcool cette année
france24fr.description: Le Comité champagne a annoncé mercredi avoir obtenu l'autorisation de commercialisation de bouteilles à plus de 13 % d'alcool, une première. Il a également estimé que cette vendange 2026 marquée par le gel, la sécheresse et des vagues de chaleur présente cette année "un potentiel de très grands vins".

france24fr.title: "C’est un vaste chantier" : après le vol de deux Renoir, le défi de la sécurité des musées français
france24fr.description: Le cambriolage du musée Renoir de Cagnes-sur-Mer survenu mardi vient allonger la liste des vols d’œuvres d’art commis ces dernières années en France. Un phénomène qui met en lumière la vulnérabilité des collections et relance le débat sur les moyens consacrés à la sécurité des musées et à la lutte contre le trafic de biens culturels.

france24fr.title: Gambie : la colère monte après plusieurs semaines de coupures d'électricité
france24fr.description: 🇬🇲 En Gambie, des milliers de personnes ont manifesté contre les coupures d’électricité qui se prolongent depuis plusieurs semaines. Ils ont bloqué des routes et brûlé des pneus pour dénoncer l’inaction du gouvernement.

france24fr.title: En Inde, l'aviation civile en plein essor
france24fr.description: L'Inde est devenue le troisième marché aérien mondial derrière la Chine et les États-Unis. Le pays a vu la construction de plus de 70 aéroports en dix ans. Une croissance spectaculaire, de quoi attirer les investissements étrangers et de grands fleurons de l'aéronautique comme Airbus, qui a conquis plus de 70 % de la flotte indienne. Mais pour répondre à ces besoins, il va également falloir former beaucoup de pilotes. Reportage d'Alban Alvarez et Sacha Desmaizières.

france24fr.title: Serbie : le président Vucic dissout le Parlement et convoque des législatives anticipées
france24fr.description: Le président serbe a annoncé mercredi la dissolution du Parlement, en réponse à un mouvement de protestations né de l'effondrement meurtrier d'un auvent dans la gare de Novi Sad fin 2024. Aleksandar Vucic a convoqué des législatives anticipées pour le 25 octobre, des élections qui pourraient le projeter à nouveau au poste de Premier ministre.

france24fr.title: Céline Dion, l'hymne à la France
france24fr.description: Deux ans après son "Hymne à l'amour" sur la tour Eiffel lors des Jeux olympiques, Céline Dion revient avec une série de concerts à Paris. L'euphorie est telle que les fans en oublient presque que Céline est Canadienne et non Française. Une histoire d'amour qui dure depuis quatre décennies.

france24fr.title: Tunisie : les journalistes appellent à la libération d'un confrère
france24fr.description: Ce mardi 8 septembre, plusieurs dizaines de journalistes tunisiens ont manifesté à Tunis pour réclamer la libération de leur confrère Mohamed Yousfi, arrêté pour "enrichissement illégal" et "blanchiment d'argent", des accusations que son avocate qualifie d'infondées. Il a été arrêté alors qu'il allait participer à une émission radio, au cours de laquelle il devait évoquer la crise de l'eau.

france24fr.title: La Gambie manifeste face aux coupures d'électricité prolongées
france24fr.description: Des milliers de personnes ont manifesté spontanément dans la nuit du lundi 7 au mardi 8 septembre dans les principales villes de Gambie. Les habitants expriment leur mécontentement contre le gouvernement après des semaines de coupures d'électricité prolongées, poussant le président gambien à s'adresser à la nation mardi soir.

france24fr.title: Cameroun : Maurice Kamto cède à la fronde et démissionne de la présidence du MRC
france24fr.description: L'opposant Maurice Kamto n'est plus président du parti Mouvement pour la Renaissance du Cameroun. Il a annoncé sa démission ce mardi, suite notamment à une fronde interne. Plus de détails avec notre correspondant, Marcel Amoko.

france24fr.title: Classement Pisa : comment enrayer la baisse du niveau des élèves ?
france24fr.description: L'enquête Pisa n'est plus seulement le classement de performances scolaires. Elle est devenue le révélateur d'un décrochage qui s'installe. Dans une grande partie des pays de l'OCDE, le niveau des élèves baisse. La France n'échappe pas à ce recul. Derrière les chiffres, une question se pose : pourquoi l'école peine-t-elle, année après année, à inverser la tendance ?

france24fr.title: Sénégal : la gestion de la dette, priorité du Premier ministre Lô devant l'Assemblée
france24fr.description: Le Premier ministre sénégalais Ahmadou Al Aminou Lô a fait ce mardi sa déclaration de politique générale devant le parlement. Une assemblée acquise en majorité au Pastef d'Ousmane Sonko, son prédécesseur. Lô a évoqué l'accord avec le FMI promet de redresser l'économie du Sénégal, mais parle de sacrifices. Un ajustement structurel a même été évoqué. Précisions du correspondant de France 24 à Dakar, Élimane Ndao.

france24fr.title: Moyen-Orient : l’Iran riposte après des frappes américaines
france24fr.description: Les Gardiens de la Révolution, armée idéologique de l'Iran, ont dit mercredi avoir attaqué une base militaire des Etats-Unis en Jordanie ainsi qu'une vingtaine de bateaux dans le Golfe, en réponse à des frappes américaines contre des pétroliers iraniens.

france24fr.title: À Paris, l'Europe tente de rattraper SpaceX et les États-Unis
france24fr.description: Il a été voulu par le président Emmanuel Macron lui-même : le sommet de l'Espace s'ouvre ce mercredi à Paris. L’objectif : tenter de contrecarrer les hégémonies américaine et chinoise dans le domaine. Mais les Européens ont pour le moment bien du mal à se coordonner… Récit de Jules Boiteau.

Energie: KI-Zentrum und Batteriespeicher: Neue Pläne für AKW-Standort
Notfälle: Grenze zur Schweiz dicht: Polizei prüft Auto auf Sprengstoff
Generaldebatte im Bundestag: Ein bisschen Haushalt und viel AfD in der Generaldebatte
zeit.description: Nach dem AfD-Sieg ringt Schwarz-Rot bei der Generaldebatte um den richtigen Kurs. Und: Wie stabil ist die Brandmauer der CDU in Sachsen-Anhalt?

zeit.title: Idee aus Wien: Bienen im Magdeburger Dom liefern ersten Honig
Fußball-Bundesliga: Bis 2030: Profivertrag für Münchner Mittelfeldtalent Binder
Autoversicherung: Überhöhte Werkstattkosten – BGH entlastet Kaskoversicherer
Vereinigte Arabische Emirate: Deutschland und Emirate wollen Beziehungen stark ausbauen
zeit.description: Die Bundesregierung plant mehrere milliardenschwere Abkommen mit den Vereinigten Arabischen Emiraten. Dabei geht es etwa um Investitionen, Energie, Verteidigung und KI.

zeit.title: Krisenübung: 130 Menschen üben Einsatz bei Extremwetterszenario
In Aachen: Stromnetz-Angriff: Tatverdächtiger kommt in U-Haft
»Oasis – Don’t Look Back in Anger«: Versöhnung unterm Anglerhut
zeit.description: In der Oasis-Doku »Don’t Look Back in Anger« werden die verfeindeten Brüder Liam und Noel Gallagher wieder Freunde. Was für Deppen, was für eine Story.

zeit.title: Briefwahl in Berlin: Briefwahlunterlagen für falschen Wahlkreis in Berlin versandt
zeit.description: Im Berliner Bezirk Charlottenburg-Wilmersdorf haben Wähler Stimmzettel für den falschen Wahlbezirk erhalten. Es könnten bis zu 1.400 Wahlberechtigte betroffen sein.

zeit.title: Psychische Gesundheit in der Schweiz: Je älter, desto glücklicher
zeit.description: Wer in der Schweiz die Pubertät überstanden hat, kann sich auf ein erfülltes Leben freuen, sagt die Statistik. Gute Aussichten, oder?

zeit.title: Anschlag auf das World Trade Center: Der Mann in der Wolke
zeit.description: Sein Vater Sebastian Gorki starb beim Anschlag auf das World Trade Center, ein halbes Jahr vor Nicholas’ Geburt. Wie lebt es sich mit diesem Erbe?

zeit.title: Konzerte gegen rechts: Spart euch die Predigt
zeit.description: Das Festival Glücksgefühle will unpolitisch sein und lädt Alphaville aus, während andere Bands vergeblich gegen die AfD ansingen. Zur Zukunft des Popkonzerts gegen rechts

spiegel.title: DFB-Pokal in Mannheim: Ermittlungen gegen Polizisten nach Pyro-Vorfall
spiegel.description: Beim Pokalspiel zwischen Mannheim und Kaiserslautern war es zu Ausschreitungen gekommen. Weil ein Polizist einen Feuerwerkskörper zurück auf die Tribüne geworfen haben soll, wird nun ermittelt.

spiegel.title: Königs Wusterhausen: Ermittler finden menschlichen Schädel
spiegel.description: Er soll bis zu 30 Jahre alt sein und wurde noch nie bestattet: In Königs Wusterhausen haben Ermittler einen rätselhaften Schädel gefunden. Womöglich wurde er Menschen zum Verkauf angeboten.

spiegel.title: Kfz-Versicherung: Vollkasko muss überhöhte Reparaturkosten nicht voll tragen
spiegel.description: Nach einem Unfall stellen manche Autowerkstätten zu viel in Rechnung – oft weigern sich Versicherungen trotz Vollkasko, die Mehrkosten zu übernehmen. Zu Recht, entschied nun der Bundesgerichtshof.

spiegel.title: Basketball-WM der Frauen: Deshalb spielt Deutschland gerade so stark
spiegel.description: Nach drei Siegen in Folge stehen die deutschen Basketballerinnen bei der WM im Viertelfinale. Das Team hat zwar eine Schwäche – aber auch viele Stärken. Ist sogar eine Medaille möglich?

spiegel.title: Annalena Baerbock: Was New York mit der Ex-Außenministerin gemacht hat
spiegel.description: Als Außenministerin war sie Zielscheibe von Hass und Häme, nun hört sie als Uno-Diplomatin auf. Was New York mit Annalena Baerbock gemacht hat – und was sie mit New York.

spiegel.title: Claudia Obert: Unternehmerin und Reality-TV-Teilnehmerin rechnet mit Merz und CDU ab
spiegel.description: Mehrere Jahre war sie Mitglied in der CDU. Nach dem AfD-Wahlsieg in Sachsen-Anhalt ist damit offenbar Schluss. Claudia Obert, bekannt aus Reality-TV-Formaten, findet deutliche Worte gegen die Partei und ihren Kanzler.

spiegel.title: Bayern: Radfahrer von Forstmaschine erfasst und getötet
spiegel.description: Trotz Warnschildern fuhr ein Senior mit seinem Pedelec in einen abgesperrten Bereich. Dort überrollte ihn ein Forstfahrzeug. Er starb noch vor Ort.

spiegel.title: Ratko Mladić: Serbien verherrlicht einen Kriegsverbrecher – und Europa schaut hilflos zu
spiegel.description: In Belgrad verabschiedeten sich Tausende vom »Schlächter vom Balkan«, darunter auch amtierende Minister der serbischen Regierung. Hat sich ein EU-Beitritt des Landes damit erledigt?

spiegel.title: Norwegen: König Harald V. in Oslo beerdigt - Marius Borg Høiby vor Ort
spiegel.description: In Oslo hat das Staatsbegräbnis für König Harald begonnen. Zehntausende Menschen schauen zu. Auch der Bundespräsident begleitete den Trauerzug.

spiegel.title: Laura Dahlmeier posthum in Hall of Fame des deutschen Sports aufgenommen
spiegel.description: Im vergangenen Jahr verunglückte Laura Dahlmeier bei einer Bergtour im Karakorum. Nun wurde sie für ihre herausragende sportliche Leistung geehrt. Auch andere Sportpersönlichkeiten ziehen in die Hall of Fame ein.

spiegel.title: Freiburg: Ermittler vermuten hinter Messerangriffen denselben Täter
spiegel.description: Zwei Menschen in Freiburg wurden in kurzer Zeit Opfer von Messerattacken. Ein 74-Jähriger starb. Laut Polizei und Staatsanwaltschaft dürfte derselbe Mann hinter den Taten stecken.

spiegel.title: Kurzzeitvermietung: EU-Kommission will Regeln für Airbnb und Co. verschärfen
spiegel.description: In beliebten Reisezielen wie Paris oder Barcelona sorgen Plattformen wie Airbnb für Druck auf dem Immobilienmarkt. Nun will die EU neue Regeln einführen, um den Ferienwohnungsboom zu bremsen.

spiegel.title: Steffen Krach: Hausdurchsuchung bei SPD-Spitzenkandidat in Berlin und Hannover
spiegel.description: Gegen den Berliner SPD-Spitzenkandidaten Steffen Krach wird wegen des Verdachts der Bestechlichkeit ermittelt. Es gab Durchsuchungen an drei Orten. Die SPD bestreitet die Vorwürfe.

spiegel.title: Polen: Wie wird der AfD-Wahlsieg gesehen? »Man bekommt hier Gänsehaut«
spiegel.description: Auch in Polen reagieren viele Menschen sorgenvoll auf den AfD-Triumph in Sachsen-Anhalt. Die bekannte Podcasterin Anna Kwiatkowska sagt, was sie besonders beunruhigt.

spiegel.title: Ukraine und Russland: Tote nach Drohnenangriffen in Cherson und Noworossijsk
spiegel.description: Russische Drohnenangriffe töten zwei Bewohner der südukrainischen Großstadt Cherson. Die Ukraine greift derweil den Sitz der russischen Schwarzmeerflotte an. Dort sterben vier Menschen.

spiegel.title: Sachsen-Anhalt live: Nur BSW nimmt AfD-Einladung zu Sondierungsgesprächen an
spiegel.description: Eine Mehrheit im Magdeburger Landtag wird es für die AfD wohl nur mit dem BSW geben. Alle anderen Parteien lehnen Gespräche dazu ab. Und: Eine Linke soll die konstituierende Sitzung des Parlaments leiten. Die Entwicklungen im Newsblog.

spiegel.title: Matterhorn: Kalie McCrystal wollte einen Rekord aufstellen. Nun fehlt jede Spur von ihr
spiegel.description: Bergretter suchen am Matterhorn verzweifelt nach der berühmten Trailrunnerin Kalie McCrystal. Gibt es noch Hoffnung, die Kanadierin lebend zu finden?

spiegel.title: Thüringen: BSW-Abtrünnige gründen neue Fraktion im Landtag
spiegel.description: Zehn Ex-BSWler wollen in Erfurt weiter mitregieren. Als Thüringen.Gerecht-Fraktion unterstützen sie fortan die Regierung von CDU-Ministerpräsident Mario Voigt.

nzz.title: Wohnungsnot wegen Airbnb? Die EU-Kommission will das Problem mit einer Zauberformel lösen
nzz.description: Für Brüssel sind Kurzzeitvermietungen mitverantwortlich, dass in Tourismus-Hotspots die lokale Bevölkerung verdrängt wird. Doch der Widerstand gegen neue Regulierung zeichnet sich bereits ab.

nzz.title: Schweizer Schüler werden immer schlechter – obwohl die Bildungsausgaben steigen: Weshalb mehr Geld nicht zu besseren Pisa-Resultaten führt
nzz.description: Vor allem die Ergebnisse beim Lesen sind teilweise ernüchternd: Die Schule scheint Mühe zu haben, den Kompetenzverlust aufzufangen. An den Ressourcen kann es nicht liegen.

nzz.title: Zwei Tote nach Explosion in Kraftwerk: «schwerer Arbeitsunfall» im Kanton Tessin
nzz.description: Im Wasserkraftwerk Ritom in Piotta kam es am Mittwochmorgen zu einem Brand, der zwei Arbeiter das Leben kostete. Die Ursache für die Explosion ist noch unklar.

nzz.title: Kiew ist so schutzlos gegen Moskaus Luftangriffe wie seit Jahren nicht – und seine Bewohner sind einsamer geworden
nzz.description: Nach einer kurzen Waffenruhe setzt Russland seine Attacken gegen die Ukraine unerbittlich fort. Der Alltag in der Hauptstadt schwankt zwischen Alarmstimmung und Stillstand.

nzz.title: KURZMELDUNGEN - News aus Zürich: Selbstfahrende Shuttlebusse am Flughafen sind neu ohne Sicherheitspersonal unterwegs
nzz.description: Die neuesten Meldungen aus dem Kanton.

nzz.title: BILDSTRECKE - König Harald V. wird in Oslo beigesetzt – die Bilder
nzz.description: Sein Volk nannte ihn liebevoll «Grossvater von ganz Norwegen»: Beim Staatsbegräbnis von König Harald V. nahmen Royals, Präsidenten, Hunderte Journalisten und viele Norweger teil.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Erinnerungskultur ist nicht überflüssig – sie hält Wunden offen, die offen bleiben müssen
nzz.description: Am Dienstag, 81 Jahre und 4 Monate nach dem Ende des Zweiten Weltkriegs, hat der Bund in Bern das Siegerprojekt für das erste nationale Memorial für die Opfer des Nationalsozialismus vorgestellt. Es hat lange gedauert.

nzz.title: DATENANALYSE - Das sind die letzten grünen Inseln im AfD-Land
nzz.description: In Sachsen-Anhalt dominiert die Farbe Blau – mit zwei Ausnahmen. Welchen Anteil hatten sie an der verpassten absoluten Mehrheit?

nzz.title: KURZMELDUNGEN - Wirtschaft: Zimmer Biomet will bis zu 580 Stellen in Winterthur abbauen
Bundesrat will schnelles Internet in die Randgebiete bringen
nzz.description: Wo sich der Ausbau von Breitbandnetzen für Anbieter nicht lohnt, droht ein digitales Defizit. Der Bundesrat beantragt deshalb einen Verpflichtungskredit in Höhe von 365 Millionen Franken.

nzz.title: LIVE-TICKER - Iran-Krieg: Tanker mit irakischem Öl gerät ins Kreuzfeuer +++ Angriffe im Nahen Osten treiben Rohölpreis über 100 Dollar
nzz.description: Die USA und Iran befinden sich seit Februar 2026 im Kriegszustand. Zwar haben die beiden Länder eine Waffenruhe vereinbart, doch Donald Trump hat diese Anfang Juli für beendet erklärt. Die neuesten Entwicklungen im Ticker.

nzz.title: Alkohol, Milch und Motorräder: Trump will Amerikaner mit Importverboten vom Konsum kanadischer Waren abhalten
nzz.description: Die Vereinigten Staaten verbieten die Einfuhr weiterer Produkte aus Kanada. Doch der Handelskonflikt mit dem Nachbarland könnte für die Republikaner bei den Zwischenwahlen zum Problem werden.

nzz.title: Die Comicserie «South Park» heisst jetzt «South America»
nzz.description: Die Produzenten reagieren auf Trumps Geografie-Gelüste. Die Umbenennung zeigt auch, dass die Wirklichkeit die Satire überholt hat.

nzz.title: KURZMELDUNGEN - Polizei-News aus Zürich: Motorradfahrer bei Kollision schwer verletzt
nzz.description: Die neusten Polizeimeldungen aus der Region.

observador.title: Contas equilibradas "têm grande valor na vida das pessoas"
observador.description: Governo aprovou prolongamento do apoio ao gasóleo agrícola e remeteu para a próxima semana decisão sobre ajudas a outros setores. Montenegro defendeu "decisões ousadas do ponto de vista orçamental".

observador.title: EUA fazem bomba de nova geração para instalações nucleares
observador.description: EUA estarão a desenvolver nova arma para atacar instalações nucleares no Irão em profundidade. Imagens mostram "claro aumento na atividade de construção em 2026".

observador.title: O que a estética não conta sobre a saúde das unhas
observador.description: Gel, verniz permanente, muitas são as técnicas de embelezamento das unhas, mas pouco se sabe sobre os efeitos. Os dermatologistas Dr. António Massa e Dra. Rita Guedes falaram sobre a saúde das unhas.

observador.title: Daimler Truck vai fechar centro tecnológico tb.lx em Lisboa
observador.description: A Daimler vai encerrar o centro tecnológico de Lisboa, que instalou no país em 2018. Decisão afeta cem trabalhadores.

observador.title: “Na província não se sentia tanto a opressão do regime”
observador.description: Henrique Araújo, ex-presidente do Supremo Tribunal de Justiça, recorda o período revolucionário do 25 de Abril, os primeiros tempos como juiz e as reformas que a administração da Justiça necessita.

observador.title: Colisão entre comboio e camião faz um morto e 19 feridos
observador.description: Acidente ocorreu numa passagem de nível em Sokolniki Suche. Seis carruagens saíram dos carris. Maquinista e condutor do camião estão entre os quatro feridos graves. Tusk promete apertar segurança.

observador.title: "Projeto tem pechas, é anacrónico e está desadequado"
observador.description: Benfica SAD apresentou resultados positivos pela segunda época seguida, agora de 19,1 milhões, com subida do ativo, do passivos e dos capitais próprios. No entanto, o grande foco atual na Luz é outro.

observador.title: Lula pede suspensão de afastamento de dirigentes da Polícia
observador.description: Juiz André Mendonça afastou dos cargos o diretor-geral da Polícia Federal e o diretor de Inteligência da corporação por ter sido alvo de "monitoramento sistemático" e "ilícito".

observador.title: Homem condenado por usar app da Tesla para ameaçar ex-mulher
observador.description: Enrico Pucci manipulou o Tesla da ex-mulher, alterando temperaturas, limitando velocidade e bloqueando o acesso. Declarou-se culpado de 30 crimes de violência doméstica praticados durante quatro anos.

observador.title: 15h.Governo aprova novos modelos de colocação de professores
observador.description: Medida anunciada na reunião do Conselho de Ministros. Ainda, Ministra da Justiça pede para apurar quantos materiais estavam incluídos no orçamento feito pela PJ durante os mandatos de Luís Neves.

observador.title: Instituto Camões promete valorizar salários de docentes
observador.description: A presidente do Instituto Camões garante que quer apostar na "valorização das carreiras e remuneratória dos professores do Ensino de Português no Estrangeiro", destacando o seu papel no ensino.

observador.title: Seixal. Corrida e caminhada pela construção de hospital
observador.description: Construção da unidade de saúde é uma reivindicação com mais de duas décadas que já foi objeto de um protocolo entre o Estado e a Câmara Municipal, em 2009, com inauguração prevista para 2012.

observador.title: Pais reclamam 500 mil euros pela morte de filho em baliza
observador.description: Um aluno de 15 morreu após a queda de uma baliza durante a aula de educação física. Os pais do menino pedem quase 500 mil euros ao professor e à congregação religiosa responsável pela escola.

observador.title: Santa Maria da Feira assina 1.º acordo de Empregador Público
observador.description: Acordo foi assinado com mais quatro estruturas sindicais e vem atualizar diferentes matérias da relação laboral tais como a redução do período experimental, e o aumento do crédito de horas.

observador.title: Universidade de Turismo de Macau reforça internacionalização
observador.description: A Universidade de Turismo de Macau quer formar docentes moçambicanos e negoceia ainda colaboração com Angola. MGM China financia a expansão com 106 mil euros.

observador.title: Vicens alerta para "poder de ataque" do Estrela da Amadora
observador.description: O Sporting de Braga vem de uma vitória por 1-2 no terreno do Alverca, enquanto os amadorenses de um empate caseiro com o Famalicão (2-2), sendo que ainda não perderam no campeonato.

observador.title: Menezes quer fim de pórtico da A29 no Orçamento de Estado
observador.description: O autarca pede que todas as forças políticas no Parlamento aprovem a medida, de "inteira justiça e equidade social" e acusa o PS de nunca reivindicar publicamente a eliminação daquele pórtico.

Over the years, researchers have caught snippets of these exchanges, but the complete dialogue has remained out of reach.

phys-org.title: Hidden microplastic pollution in Swiss waters uncovered
phys-org.description: Microplastics are plastic particles smaller than 5 millimeters that originate either from manufactured products or from the breakdown of larger plastic items. They can now be found everywhere, from oceans and rivers to soils and indoor air. Because most plastics degrade very slowly, these particles can remain in the environment for decades or centuries.

phys-org.title: More than numbers: First global dataset shows who is immigrating
phys-org.description: As countries compete for skilled workers and grapple with aging populations and labor shortages, understanding who is moving across borders is increasingly important. A new study provides the first global data set of immigration composition disaggregated simultaneously by age, sex and educational attainment, offering a new basis for tracking brain gain and brain drain and improving population projections.

phys-org.title: Ancient bones reveal that cannibalism took different forms in Neolithic Spain
phys-org.description: Cannibalism was sometimes on the Neolithic menu, as numerous archaeological discoveries have revealed. Was it to stave off hunger during times of desperation? Did different tribes eat their defeated enemies? Or was cannibalism part of complex rituals?

undark.title: Book Review: The Messy Business of Making Science Happen
undark.description: In “Lost in Curiosity: Field Notes From Scientists’ Adventures Into the Unknown,” Roberta Kwok sets out to smash the stereotype of eureka moments as the main drivers of scientific knowledge, largely by taking us inside the everyday world of science and scientists, in all its painstaking monotony.

undark.title: Book Review: Our Conflicted Relationship with the Sun
undark.description: Despite dermatological guidelines that decree sunlight a harmful carcinogen, Rowan Jacobsen argues in “In Defense of Sunlight” that the sun helps our skin produce many compounds vital to our health. How did science miss these benefits? The answer, he says, lies in our inability to do things in moderation.

undark.title: The New Student Visa Policy Doesn’t Add Up
undark.description: In July, the Department of Homeland Security issued new rules that would make it harder for international students to complete their studies in the U.S. The policy threatens to be disruptive for students — particularly doctoral candidates — and self-defeating for the country.

undark.title: Book Review: How Wildlife Is Returning to the East
undark.description: In “The Beasts of the East,” journalist Andrew Moore charts the natural history of the East and the people who have dedicated their careers to restoring several long lost species to what remains of their original habitats.

undark.title: Book Review: The Case for the AI-Powered Global Brain
undark.description: In “The God Test,” Robert Wright considers a future in which human consciousness becomes infused with AI. “We have to think seriously about a future in which there is something that increasingly resembles a global brain, and its neurons increasingly consist not just of human brains but of AIs,” he writes.

undark.title: Interview: How Tragedy Changed the FDA
undark.description: As an FDA advisory committee prepares to weigh whether specialized pharmacies should be allowed to dispense seven unapproved peptides, Mikkael A. Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

undark.title: The MAHA Movement’s Worrisome Embrace of Ibogaine
undark.description: The MAHA movement has been promoting the plant-based substance ibogaine as a remedy for opioid addiction, despite the lack of clinical trials on its safety and efficacy. One physician who practices addiction medicine discusses the risks of ibogaine and argues for the need to support proven treatments.

proj-syn.title: Europe Needs Dual-Use Defense Spending
proj-syn.description: Some EU countries, such as Poland, are using their expanded defense budgets to buy more foreign hardware. A better approach would be to foster a thriving innovation ecosystem which ensures that the technologies, institutions, and people that underpin a strong military benefit the civilian economy as well.

proj-syn.title: The World 9/11 Didn’t Make
proj-syn.description: Looking back at the past quarter-century, it becomes apparent that the 9/11 terrorist attack against the United States was not a transformative event. Far more important developments have intervened, not least America’s rejection of the postwar order that it had a large hand in building.

proj-syn.title: The BRICS at 20
proj-syn.description: If the promise of the BRICS was to establish a monetary union, a single market, or a tightly integrated political alliance, it has not been fulfilled. But if it was to build a platform for emerging economies to cooperate while advancing their own strategic autonomy, the BRICS has exceeded expectations.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s Security Depends on a Clear Electrification Target
proj-syn.description: The politics around electrification are beginning to shift in Europe as more people recognize its importance for economic competitiveness and industrial resilience. European Union policymakers should seize this momentum to embed a binding target of at least 50% electrification by 2040 in the bloc’s energy security framework.

proj-syn.title: The AI Race Could Sink US-China Détente
proj-syn.description: The competition between the United States and China to develop AI and deploy it globally poses the biggest threat to the two countries’ currently constructive relations. Without an ongoing AI dialogue to avoid escalation, a return to the zero-sum conflict that rattled both sides last year cannot be ruled out.

proj-syn.title: Are China’s Rare Earths Really a Potent Weapon?
proj-syn.description: The available evidence indicates that Chinese rare-earth export restrictions would cost the West far less than often feared, though this cost is impossible to estimate precisely in advance. This is forcing prudence on both sides, to the disappointment of geopolitical hawks and the benefit of the global economy.

proj-syn.title: The Trump Shock in East Asia
proj-syn.description: US President Donald Trump has alarmed his East Asian allies by canceling two joint military exercises with South Korea, a move that seems motivated less by whim than by a fondness for tyrants. The question now is whether South Korea and Japan will set aside historical resentments for the sake of mutual interests.

proj-syn.title: Building a Resilient Nepal
proj-syn.description: After Japan’s 2011 Fukushima nuclear disaster, the Japanese government changed the building codes for schools and housing and rethought the placement of critical infrastructure. Nepal (and other vulnerable countries) must pursue a similar approach.

proj-syn.title: Unpaid Work in the AI Age
proj-syn.description: Unpaid work, such as dealing with government bureaucracy and private-sector administration, consumes a huge amount of people's free time. While AI tools have the potential to change this, with important implications for the economy, predictions about AI’s impact tend to focus exclusively on paid work.

proj-syn.title: The Digital Wellness Industry Is Hijacking Women’s Health
proj-syn.description: Menopause and perimenopause, long under-researched and dismissed, have become a growth industry for online advertisers and wellness companies. Mining intimate data, this lucrative digital ecosystem exploits medical uncertainty to sell women hormones and supplements they don't need, or that can even harm them.

proj-syn.title: Who Controls the Data Controls the Future
proj-syn.description: While AI is becoming increasingly central to finance, defense, health care, and public administration, it depends on resources most governments do not control: the data used to train it and the compute that processes it. Unless this changes, countries will remain subject to decisions made in boardrooms they cannot influence.

proj-syn.title: Will Europe Be as Unprepared as Ukraine Was?
proj-syn.description: With Russia ramping up its hybrid war, Europe must choose. It can invest in its own defense, accept the trade-offs involved, and build credible deterrence, or it can continue to underspend, hope that diplomacy will suffice, assume that US protection will always be available, and tell itself that the war in Ukraine is a local affair.

proj-syn.title: The Case for a Cashflow Tax
proj-syn.description: In the context of the US economy, a cashflow tax would offer far-reaching benefits in promoting economic growth, taxing rents, and raising incremental revenue efficiently. Moreover, well-known concerns about complexity and fairness are easily addressed.

proj-syn.title: Kevin Warsh’s Best Move Is to Do Nothing
proj-syn.description: Beholden to mainstream economic ideas, the new US Federal Reserve chair has committed himself, and his reputation, to a goal he cannot achieve. Reining in inflation requires not interest-rate adjustments but much larger strategic shifts that are not within the Fed’s power to influence.

proj-syn.title: How Developing Countries Can Do More With Less
proj-syn.description: Evaluation frameworks for development projects have long been influenced by donor priorities. But foreign-aid cuts have created an opportunity for African countries to implement equitable evaluation practices, both to channel limited resources more effectively and to shape the future of global development governance.

proj-syn.title: America’s Naval Disaster
proj-syn.description: Plagued by exorbitant costs and chronic delays, American shipbuilders cannot produce enough vessels to keep pace with China. US President Donald Trump’s push to rebuild the industry does little to address its underlying problems and threatens to squander hundreds of billions of dollars.

proj-syn.title: America’s Un-American AI Companies
proj-syn.description: The United States can prevail in the AI race against China by leaning into the strengths of an open society: democratic oversight, the rule of law, robust competition, and open public debate. But that won’t happen as long as American AI companies aggressively lobby against accountability and cozy up to the state.

proj-syn.title: The Golden Bridge to Monetary Multipolarity
proj-syn.description: Gold has overtaken US Treasuries as the world’s top reserve asset because it offers a solution to the challenges of a rogue America. But its renewed relevance also reflects how rapid technological diffusion and increasing dispersion of economic power are creating a more diversified international monetary system.
